correctness.rationale: At each convex polyhedral vertex, orient faces outward and label the three distinct side lengths modulo 3. The common cyclic label sequence forces each consecutive radial edge color to advance 2 mod 3, hence the vertex valence d is divisible by 3. Every three consecutive incident corners are the three angles of T once, so incident angle sum equals d*pi/3; strict convexity (<2pi) and d>=3 force d=3. Euler and triangulation counting yield V=F=4, E=6. Each side length appears on exactly two opposite tetrahedron edges, so P is disphenoid. The standard orthogonal coordinate realization gives x²=(b²+c²-a²)/8 etc, positive iff T acute, and uniform outward handedness by half-turn symmetries. The conclusion is an unrestricted combinatorial/convex proof; finite tetra/octa oriented-color verifier only corroborates.
residual_risks: The notion of orientation preserving is explicitly with respect to outward surface orientation, not unrestricted 3D proper rotation of planar subsets. Convexity and genuine facets essential.

originality.rationale: Georgiou (2026) classifies reflection-allowed congruent triangular facets, cites direct orientation as remaining open for right/obtuse scalene triangles; his acute tetrahedron converse is credited. Hungerbühler et al construct monohedral shapes with reflected facet arrangements, and the exact scalene octahedron classification is only an 8-face reflection-allowed finite case. Neither entails the all-face-count one-handed exclusion. The local modulo-three valence/curvature obstruction is not located as a previously published theorem.
